note: The authoritative wording lives in strategy §10 (which amends SRS §13). This file maps each criterion to the named tests that prove it. `phase` says when it can first be proved; a criterion with no tests yet must say why.

criteria.title: Golden masters map byte for byte, display included
tests: golden masters (fake provider) property/basic
golden masters (fake provider) property/no-references
golden masters (fake provider) office/basic
golden masters (fake provider) agent/basic
golden masters (fake provider) area/basic
golden masters (fake provider) association/basic
criteria.note: Proved on golden/fake, whose cases now cover identity, references and dummy fake_* fields only. display is empty in every case because no business rule exists. Real per-CRM golden masters arrive at Gate 3.

criteria.title: An unchanged record produces no new seq and no bell
tests: ingest gives an unchanged record no new seq and no bell (AC 15)
two adapters, one engine writes nothing new when a poll finds no change (AC 15)

criteria.title: A change gives one new seq; a gone record becomes a tombstone
tests: ingest gives a real change a new seq and logs what changed
ingest tombstones a record the CRM no longer has (AC 26)
two adapters, one engine tombstones through presentIds when a polled record disappears (AC 35)
the Vitec adapter tombstones after a Remove notification once Vitec answers 404 (AC 3)

criteria.title: The cursor returns everything from 0 and only changes after that
tests: GET /v1/changes returns everything from seq 0 and only newer items after that (AC 4)
GET /v1/changes caps a page at the page size and says there is more

criteria.title: A subscriber converges from 0, from a cursor, and on forcerefresh
tests: a subscriber converges from seq 0 to everything Core holds (AC 5)
a subscriber carries on from its cursor and pulls nothing when nothing changed
a subscriber rebuilds its whole copy on forcerefresh (AC 5)
a subscriber drops an item locally when Core tombstones it

criteria.title: Two connections of one provider under one tenant do not collide
tests: identity keeps two connections of one provider apart, even with the same remote id (AC 6)

criteria.title: Tenant isolation and the admin secret
tests: GET /v1/changes refuses an unknown token, a missing token and a tenant_id parameter
admin needs the admin secret
criteria.note: Cross-tenant reads are blocked by the token-to-tenant lookup; a second tenant fixture would make that explicit.

criteria.title: Core down: client sites keep serving
tests: the Lovable kit against Core keeps its copy and reports the failure when Core is down (AC 8)
the WordPress client against Core keeps its copy and reports the failure when Core is down (AC 8)
criteria.note: The sync half, on both real clients: the local copy stays and the failure is reported. Page rendering through a 24 h outage needs templates and a staging site.

criteria.title: licensed_offices limits what exists in Core
tests: ingest drops a record from an unlicensed office and says why (AC 9)

criteria.title: An added field reaches subscribers and breaks nothing
tests: the Lovable kit against Core stores a field it has never seen, verbatim (AC 10, AC 30)
the WordPress client against Core stores a field it has never seen, verbatim (AC 10, AC 30)
criteria.note: Both real clients store an item with a field they have never seen, verbatim, and keep going. The engine half is that data is stored and served verbatim.

criteria.title: A malformed record is dropped, logged, and blocks nothing
tests: ingest drops one malformed record and still writes the others (AC 11)
criteria.note: Reported to the event log. Sentry reporting waits on the DSN.

criteria.title: An invented provider works end to end; no CRM name in the engine
tests: two adapters, one engine serves items from both, side by side, with different payload shapes
two adapters, one engine reports the health check each adapter registered
the seam check passes on this repository
the seam check fails when the engine names a CRM

criteria.title: recompute rewrites affected records with no CRM traffic
tests: admin recomputes from stored raw with no CRM traffic, and gives a new seq (AC 13)

criteria.title: Adding an office loads only that office's records
tests: admin loads only the added office, and gives other offices no new seq (AC 14)
two adapters, one engine resyncs a connection on request (AC 14)
the Vitec adapter loads an added office without a new seq for the others (AC 14)
the Vitec adapter tombstones what Vitec no longer lists on a resync (AC 14)
criteria.note: The adapter loads the added office's records plus the tenant-wide entities they reference; other offices get no new seq.

criteria.title: replay reproduces the current records exactly
tests: admin recomputes from stored raw with no CRM traffic, and gives a new seq (AC 13)
admin previews a recompute without writing anything (AC 36)

criteria.title: The event log answers one entity's whole timeline
tests: ingest keeps the whole timeline of an entity in the event log (AC 16)
admin answers the event timeline query
ingest links a webhook to the write it caused by correlation id (AC 16)
the event log keeps every event when many writers log at once
the event log deletes events outside the retention window (AC 16)
criteria.note: Causes covered: written, unchanged, dropped (unlicensed, malformed, inactive, unknown datatype), tombstoned, bell, pull. A correlation id links a webhook to the write it caused; an adapter cannot yet stamp its own events with one (open question 9).

criteria.title: Health and alerting
tests: health is 500 while a check fails and 200 when everything passes (AC 17)
criteria.note: Sentry Uptime alerting waits on the account.

criteria.title: Pipeline: staging on merge, production on approval
criteria.note: Waits on the platform Kowboy supplies.

criteria.title: No skipped items under concurrent writes
tests: a subscriber misses no item while writes keep arriving (AC 19)
criteria.note: Proved against concurrent writes in one process. Deploy overlap needs staging.

criteria.title: Real clients pass the sync and search suites
tests: the Lovable kit against Core pulls when Core rings, and refuses a bell with the wrong secret
the WordPress client against Core pulls when Core rings, and refuses a bell with the wrong secret
the Lovable kit against Core converges from seq 0 to everything Core holds (AC 5, AC 34)
the WordPress client against Core converges from seq 0 to everything Core holds (AC 5, AC 34)
the Lovable kit against Core skips unchanged items and carries on from its cursor (AC 2)
the WordPress client against Core skips unchanged items and carries on from its cursor (AC 2)
the Lovable kit against Core drops an item locally when Core tombstones it (AC 3)
the WordPress client against Core drops an item locally when Core tombstones it (AC 3)
the Lovable kit against Core rewrites everything on forcerefresh, repairing damage a delta sync never sees (AC 5)
the WordPress client against Core rewrites everything on forcerefresh, repairing damage a delta sync never sees (AC 5)
the Lovable kit against Core stores a field it has never seen, verbatim (AC 10, AC 30)
the WordPress client against Core stores a field it has never seen, verbatim (AC 10, AC 30)
the Lovable kit against Core skips an item it cannot use, and keeps going (AC 30)
the WordPress client against Core skips an item it cannot use, and keeps going (AC 30)
the Lovable kit against Core rebuilds without ever emptying when Core says resync_required (AC 31)
the WordPress client against Core rebuilds without ever emptying when Core says resync_required (AC 31)
the Lovable kit against Core keeps its copy and reports the failure when Core is down (AC 8)
the WordPress client against Core keeps its copy and reports the failure when Core is down (AC 8)
the Lovable kit against Core misses no item while writes and bells keep coming (AC 19)
the WordPress client against Core misses no item while writes and bells keep coming (AC 19)
the Lovable kit against Core converges on its own schedule when bells never arrive (AC 22)
the WordPress client against Core converges on its own schedule when bells never arrive (AC 22)
criteria.note: The sync scenario suite (clients/sync-scenarios.ts), run as each real client against the real Core. The search/filter half needs the data model.

criteria.title: A broken client release is replaced safely
tests: the WordPress client lets the must-use updater offer a newer release without touching the plugin (AC 21)
the WordPress client packages a release WordPress can install, with the version from the plugin header
criteria.note: WordPress: the must-use updater and the release package are proved; WordPress itself swaps the plugin. Lovable: the function and the site deploy separately by construction, which no test can add to.

criteria.title: With bells blocked a subscriber converges within 15 min
tests: a subscriber converges on its own schedule when bells never arrive (AC 22)
the Lovable kit against Core converges on its own schedule when bells never arrive (AC 22)
the WordPress client against Core converges on its own schedule when bells never arrive (AC 22)
criteria.note: Proved with the fake subscriber and with both real clients’ own backstops. The 15 minute figure is a client setting.

criteria.title: Every item served validates against the schema and invariants
tests: ingest turns a webhook into a served item (AC 2, AC 3)
admin previews a recompute without writing anything (AC 36)
criteria.note: The write path refuses an item that fails its schema, and the release preview reports failures. The schemas themselves are the structural spine and permissive until the data model is defined, so today this proves the mechanism, not the model.

criteria.title: Restore drill ends with subscribers converged
Secrets and privacy
tests: the secret check passes on this repository
the secret check fails on a committed private key
the event log redacts secret-shaped fields, however deep (AC 16, AC 25)
criteria.note: Credentials are encrypted at rest and tokens are stored as an HMAC; the event log redacts secret-shaped keys. EU hosting is Kowboy's to provision.

criteria.title: Removal tombstones items; tombstones are purged after 90 days
tests: admin tombstones an office that is removed (AC 26)
ingest tombstones a record the CRM no longer has (AC 26)
tombstone retention hard-deletes a tombstone after the retention window, and keeps a fresh one (AC 26)
criteria.note: The 90 day window is proved by ageing a tombstone; the worker runs the same purge hourly.

criteria.title: Scale and read latency at 10x launch
criteria.note: Needs staging.

criteria.title: Functional parity with the parity inventory
Burst resilience (Vitec)
tests: two adapters, one engine absorbs a burst of webhooks without a fetch per webhook (AC 29 in miniature)
the Vitec adapter answers a burst of webhooks with 202 and fetches the record once (AC 29, AC 33)
criteria.note: The fake adapter and the Vitec adapter both show the shape: a burst of webhooks for one record collapses into one queued fetch, answered 202 in the request. The real figures (50,000 webhooks, p99 under 1 s) need staging.

criteria.title: Contract evolution
tests: the Lovable kit against Core stores a field it has never seen, verbatim (AC 10, AC 30)
the WordPress client against Core stores a field it has never seen, verbatim (AC 10, AC 30)
the Lovable kit against Core skips an item it cannot use, and keeps going (AC 30)
the WordPress client against Core skips an item it cannot use, and keeps going (AC 30)
criteria.note: Additive fields and unusable items on both real clients. Reporting goes to the same placeholder as Core’s until a Sentry DSN exists. The release report’s flags wait on the pipeline.

criteria.title: Purge and resync safety
tests: purge and resync safety (AC 31) tells a subscriber behind the purge watermark to resync, and it converges without ever emptying
criteria.note: Watermark and resync-required are built and proved; the rebuild swaps in only after a complete pull. Purge-and-resync as an operator action has no endpoint yet (raised as an issue).

criteria.title: Near-instant under normal load (Vitec)
Race conditions and dedupe (Vitec)
tests: two adapters, one engine absorbs a burst of webhooks without a fetch per webhook (AC 29 in miniature)
the Vitec adapter answers a burst of webhooks with 202 and fetches the record once (AC 29, AC 33)
the Vitec adapter fetches at most five records at once (proposal point 10)

criteria.title: Initial sync for a new tenant, office and subscriber
tests: admin loads a new connection end to end on connection_added (AC 34)
a subscriber converges from seq 0 to everything Core holds (AC 5)

criteria.title: Catch-up (Vitec)
tests: two adapters, one engine tombstones through presentIds when a polled record disappears (AC 35)
the Vitec adapter catches up on what changed since the last window, less one hour of overlap (AC 35)
the Vitec adapter confirms a missing id with a fetch before tombstoning it, once a day (AC 35)
criteria.note: The 12 h catch-up with its 1 h overlap and the daily id comparison are proved against a stand-in Connect; the schedule itself runs on the worker's minute tick. Vitec's live behaviour waits for a test account (open question 18).

criteria.title: Release impact preview performs no writes
tests: admin previews a recompute without writing anything (AC 36)

criteria.title: Each enforced check fails on a seeded violation
tests: the seam check fails when the engine names a CRM
the seam check fails when an adapter imports engine internals
the seam check fails when the engine imports an adapter
the seam check fails when a file other than main.ts imports both sides
the skipped-test check fails on a skipped test
the skipped-test check fails on a test that silently skips the rest of its file
the secret check fails on a committed private key

criteria.title: Webhook lag turns a check red (Vitec)
tests: the Vitec adapter turns vitec.webhook_lag red when a webhook has waited five minutes (AC 38)

criteria.title: Repeated retries turn a check red (Vitec)
tests: the Vitec adapter retries a failed fetch with backoff, turns vitec.retries red after three, and recovers (AC 39)

criteria.title: Compression
tests: GET /v1/changes gzips a full page and stays readable without gzip (AC 40)
criteria.note: Ratio and plain-JSON fallback are asserted. The under-10 ms figure needs staging.
